title: Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: We find in [Shabbat 151b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b.17) that Rabbi Yohanan spoke in his name; likewise in Sanhedrin 103b, according to the She’iltot’s reading.[^2]

Hyman also cites him in [Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 14](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.14.1); [Tanchuma, Noach 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma%2C_Noach.1.4-5) and Metzora 17; and [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.2.6.11-12), with his valuable homily on why the commandments of challah and lighting the lamp were entrusted to women. In [Rosh Hashanah 4:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.8.3), Rabbi Tachlifa of Caesarea said: Scripture says “as a day of trumpet-blowing” (כיום תרועה), “and you shall make” (ועשיתם); Rabbi Lazar bei Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta [said]: regarding all the sacrifices it is written “and you shall offer” (והקרבתם), etc. Hyman suggests that the reading should be “Rabbi Lazar in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta.” In Midrash Tehillim 78:7, Hyman cites Rabbi Shimon bar Chanan as speaking in his name.[^3][^1][^4]

notes.text: The consulted Yerushalmi reads Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Yose in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta. Hyman proposes the shorter “Rabbi Lazar in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta” for his reading of the line.
The Bavli has Rabbi Yochanan speaking in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Ketzarta. The saying about tears continues at [Shabbat 152a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.152a.1).

Bereshit Rabbah and the Yerushalmi both give the dough analogy, with ben Ketzarta and bar Ketzarta respectively. The Yerushalmi treats the lamp in the following passage. In Noach 1, Berman’s English names Yose son of Kazrata while the digital Torat Emet Hebrew reads Yose ben Dumeska.

The linked Sanhedrin passage gives Rabbi Yochanan transmitting in Rabbi Yose ben Kasma’s name. Hyman reports Ketzarta for the She’iltot witness. That reading remains unverified here. See [Sanhedrin 103b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.103b.17).
